record.paper_title: Boundary and Defect CFT: Open Problems and Applications
record.original_question: When fields Φ(ξ) on quasi Riemann surfaces are restricted to very small defects ξ that look pointlike inside the ambient 2n-dimensional manifold, do the resulting ordinary local quantum fields define genuinely new local quantum field theories in 2n dimensions?

evidence.quote: Tiny defects look like points in M, so fields Φ(ξ) when restricted to the small ξ in Q will give ordinary local quantum fields on M. Will these form new local qfts in 2n-dimensions?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Setup. Let M be a 2n-dimensional smooth manifold and let Q → M be a fiber bundle over M whose fiber at each point is a "quasi Riemann surface": a higher-dimensional generalization of a Riemann surface on which one can define a conformal-field-theory-like structure, namely an assignment to each point ξ of the total space Q of a field operator Φ(ξ) acting on a fixed Hilbert space, with operator product expansions and correlation functions analogous to those of a 2d CFT. A "defect" ξ ⊂ Q is a submanifold of Q; one says ξ is tiny (or pointlike) if its image in M under the bundle projection is concentrated near a single point of M, so that from the point of view of M the defect looks like an insertion at a point.

For each tiny defect ξ, define an ordinary local field on M by restricting/integrating the fields Φ(·) over ξ, producing an operator-valued distribution φ_ξ(x) on M (x ∈ M).

Question. Do the local fields {φ_ξ} obtained in this way, as ξ ranges over tiny defects, satisfy the Wightman/Osterwalder–Schrader axioms for a local quantum field theory on the 2n-dimensional manifold M, and if so, do they define genuinely new examples of local quantum field theories in 2n dimensions (i.e., theories not equivalent to previously known local QFTs in dimension 2n)?
artifact.status_search_result: The construction of CFT-like structures on quasi Riemann surfaces and their restriction to pointlike defects to yield local fields on a 2n-dimensional ambient manifold is a recent proposal; available references describe the construction but do not establish that the resulting restricted fields constitute new bona fide local QFTs in 2n dimensions. No proof or disproof of this claim was located, so the question appears to remain open.

status_evidence.title: A new kind of quantum field theory of (n−1)-forms
status_evidence.snippet: Construction of CFT-like fields on quasi-Riemann surfaces; restriction to small fibers yields ordinary local fields on the base manifold.
status_evidence.claim: The framework introducing quasi Riemann surfaces and pointlike defects is proposed but not established as producing new local QFTs.
